units.text: INT. BAIT SHOP - DAWN
Minnow tanks bubble in the half-dark.
A radio on the counter plays low static.
The smell of brine, worms, and old coffee.
Pale light creeps through a salt-fogged window.
LENNOX BARRETT (50s, the owner, flannel shirt, a thick scar through one eyebrow) stands behind the counter with a landline receiver clamped between ear and shoulder.
His other hand rests flat on a lockbox.
He has not slept.
The clock on the wall says 5:42.
You promised me, Lennox. You promised you'd be home before the sun came up.
units.name: MAMA PEARL

units.text: I know I did, Mama.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: I made grits. I put the pan back on the stove twice. Your sister's been here since four. She says there's a man on the dock.
units.name: MAMA PEARL

units.text: There's always a man on the dock.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: Not like this one. She says he's been standing there since midnight with his hat in his hands.
units.name: MAMA PEARL

units.text: Lennox looks out the window.
The dock is empty except for a gull.
He turns back and lifts the lid of the lockbox, and the stacks of bills inside catch the light like a pale fan.
Mama, listen to me. I'm going to put this in a bag, and I'm going to carry it out to the truck. I want you to put the phone down and go sit with Ruthie.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: Lennox, the money isn't the thing. It never was. Your father used to say a man is as much what he gives back as what he keeps.
units.name: MAMA PEARL

units.text: Daddy never kept a thing in his life.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: That's the point, baby. That's exactly the point.
units.name: MAMA PEARL

units.text: He closes the box.
He runs his thumb along the latch, once, and his shoulders drop.
Put the pan back on, Mama. Make it hot.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: I never took it off.
units.name: MAMA PEARL

units.text: He hangs up.
He carries the lockbox out through the beaded door, across the planks, to the end of the dock.
The sun lifts the edge of the water.
